§. 11. His Animi Doribus accessit justa Corporis
Statura, procera vicinior & plane virilis; congrua &
elegans membrorum proportio, in corpore aliquanto
graciliori, intra modum tamen, frons læta & porrecta,
& Oculorum masculus vigor;
vultus placidus ac
decorus, ita tamen ut Oris gratia ac venustas de
Illius vigore atque majestate nihil imminueret;
Habitus demum Gestusque totius Corporis ad sum-
mam Elegantiam compositus. Hæc item omnia deco-
rabat & multo gratiora reddebat, Educatio ingenua,
& consuetudo vitæ sermonisque cum Viris primariis
Ordinis, quibuscum Conversari solebat. Nam ut
erat vir genere Nobilis, ita & aulicis moribus infigni-
te excultus; comis erga Omnes & humanus, accessu
& alloquio facilis, officiosus in Amicos,
erga cum-

exhibuisse dicitur, adeo ut Illi crimini daretur ab
Amicis, tantus Sui Contemptus, & Aliorum Cultus.
His accessit modestus Corporis Cultus comptus ta-

longe aberat,
faciles tamen, & in promptu habendas, non asper-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "struendi" and "versipellem" in the italic phrase are hard to read in the scan and are marked [?]. "etsi" at the start of the line after "decorus" is doubtful. "adornaverint" and "infigni-te" are partly obscured by ink. The section numbers "§. 11." and "§. 12." are read from a small, blurred scan. Final word of the page continues as catchword "gentia".
